added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(k\ge1\), the rational interval oracle and dovetailed search in \(\mathrm{def:rational\text{-}airy\text{-}longitudinal\text{-}family}\) terminate and return the complete spline record specified there.  In particular,
\[
d_\dagger(\varphi_k^\dagger,\phi_{c^\dagger})^2<2^{-2k},
\qquad
\frac{4\int| (\varphi_k^\dagger)'|^2+
\kappa(c^\dagger)\int |x|(\varphi_k^\dagger)^2}
{\int(\varphi_k^\dagger)^2}
\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+2^{-k}.
\]
Thus \(\varphi_k^\dagger\to\phi_{c^\dagger}\) in weighted \(H^1\), every \(w_k^\dagger\) is a compactly supported probability density with rational piecewise-quadratic coefficients, and its normalization and normalized energy are exact rational numbers.  No oracle for an arbitrary real number is assumed: all accepted inequalities are certified by rational intervals.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(\kappa=5/8\), \(\Phi=\phi_{c^\dagger}\), and \(\Lambda=\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\).  The exact-primitives proposition gives the value of \(\kappa\), and the Airy-benchmark definition makes \(\Phi\) the positive even unit-norm minimizer of
\[
\mathcal Q(f)=4\int_{\mathbb R}|f'|^2+
\kappa\int_{\mathbb R}|x|f^2. \tag{1}
\]
Taking compactly supported variations in (1) gives the weak Euler equation
\[
-4\Phi''(x)+\kappa|x|\Phi(x)=\Lambda\Phi(x). \tag{2}
\]
Since the coefficient in (2) is continuous on each half-line, integrating the distributional equation twice shows that \(\Phi\) is \(C^2\) there.  Evenness gives \(\Phi'(0)=0\), while positivity fixes its sign.

We first prove the interval bracket used by the oracle.  On \([0,R]\), denote the Neumann and Dirichlet Rayleigh infima by \(\lambda_N(R)\) and \(\lambda_D(R)\).  Extending a Dirichlet competitor by zero gives an admissible half-line competitor, so
\[
\Lambda\le\lambda_D(R). \tag{3}
\]
For any half-line form-domain function \(f\), splitting its energy at \(R\), using the Neumann variational inequality on \([0,R]\), and using \(\kappa x\ge\kappa R\) on \([R,\infty)\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal Q_{[0,\infty)}(f)
&\ge \lambda_N(R)\int_0^R f^2+
\kappa R\int_R^\infty f^2\\
&\ge\min\{\lambda_N(R),\kappa R\}
\int_0^\infty f^2.
\end{aligned} \tag{4}
\]
Taking the infimum proves the lower bracket.  Compactly supported truncations of \(\Phi\) show from (1) that \(\lambda_D(R)\to\Lambda\).  To handle the Neumann side, take any sequence \(R_j\to\infty\) and normalized Neumann minimizers \(f_j\) with bounded energies.  For every fixed \(S\), their \(H^1(0,S)\) norms are bounded, while
\[
\int_S^{R_j}f_j^2\le\frac{\lambda_N(R_j)}{\kappa S}. \tag{5}
\]
For completeness, compactness here follows directly from the fundamental theorem of calculus.  If \(P_hg\) is the vector of cell averages on a partition of \([0,S]\) into intervals of length at most \(h\), then Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
\|g-P_hg\|_{L^2(0,S)}^2
\le h^2\|g'\|_{L^2(0,S)}^2. \tag{5a}
\]
For fixed \(h\), the finitely many cell-average vectors of the bounded sequence have a convergent subsequence; diagonal extraction as \(h\) decreases to zero and (5a) give an \(L^2(0,S)\)-convergent subsequence.  Successive extraction on integer \(S\), together with the tightness bound (5), gives a unit-norm half-line limit \(f\).  Weak lower semicontinuity of a squared norm follows from
\[
\|g\|_2^2=\sup_z\{2\langle g,z\rangle-\|z\|_2^2\},
\]
so applying this identity to \(f_j'\) and \(x^{1/2}f_j\) on each \([0,S]\), followed by monotone convergence in \(S\), yields
\[
\Lambda\le\mathcal Q(f)\le\liminf_j\lambda_N(R_j). \tag{6}
\]
Equations (4) and (6) imply \(\lambda_N(R)\to\Lambda\).  Hence the rational bracket in the definition becomes arbitrarily narrow.

For fixed rational \(R\), the initial-value equation in the definition has polynomial coefficients.  Picard's integral operator \(\mathcal P\) satisfies, on a step where \(\|A\|_\infty\le L\),
\[
\|\mathcal P^{m+1}W-\mathcal P^mW\|_\infty
\le \|W(x_0)\|_\infty
\frac{(L|h|)^{m+1}}{(m+1)!}. \tag{7}
\]
Summing (7) from \(m+1\) onward gives the displayed exponential remainder.  All coefficients and endpoints in (7) are rational intervals.  The Wronskian of two solutions satisfying the same left boundary condition is constant; consequently an eigenvalue satisfying either separated right boundary condition is simple.  If two spectral parameters are ordered, differentiating their Wronskian gives
\[
\frac{d}{dx}\{f_{\lambda_2}'f_{\lambda_1}
-f_{\lambda_2}f_{\lambda_1}'\}
=\frac{\lambda_1-\lambda_2}{4}f_{\lambda_1}f_{\lambda_2}, \tag{8}
\]
which orders the first boundary zero while both solutions are positive.  Thus a sufficiently fine rational space--parameter subdivision, interval Newton applied also to the differentiated equation, and the positivity checks isolate the first simple root.  Equations (3)--(8) prove termination of the eigenvalue-enclosure loop.

The tail formulas used by the oracle are exact.  On \([0,\infty)\), define
\[
F(x)=\Phi'(x)^2-\frac{\kappa x-\Lambda}{4}\Phi(x)^2.
\]
Equation (2) gives \(F'(x)=-\kappa\Phi(x)^2/4\).  Since the three nonnegative integrands in (1) are integrable, there is a sequence tending to infinity on which the boundary term tends to zero.  Integrating along that sequence and using \(\int_0^\infty\Phi^2=1/2\) gives
\[
\Phi(0)^2=\frac{\kappa}{2\Lambda}. \tag{9}
\]
For \(s>0\), put \(\Phi_s(x)=s^{1/2}\Phi(sx)\).  This preserves the unit norm, and minimality at \(s=1\) gives
\[
0=\left.\frac d{ds}\right|_{s=1}
\left\{4s^2\int|\Phi'|^2+
\kappa s^{-1}\int|x|\Phi^2\right\}
=8\int|\Phi'|^2-
\kappa\int|x|\Phi^2. \tag{10}
\]
Combining (1) at \(\Phi\) with (10) proves
\[
\int|\Phi'|^2=\frac{\Lambda}{12},
\qquad
\int|x|\Phi^2=\frac{2\Lambda}{3\kappa}. \tag{11}
\]
The augmented Picard system encloses the compact integrals.  Subtracting them from the exact totals (9)--(11) encloses all three tails.  Their true values tend to zero by integrability, while (7) makes the interval widths arbitrarily small.  Therefore the ODE and weighted-tail oracle terminates at every requested precision.

If \(p\) is a proposed compact spline, expansion of the squared distance gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
d_\dagger(p,\Phi)^2
={}&\int|p'|^2+\frac{\Lambda}{12}
-2\int p'\Phi'\\
&+\int(1+|x|)p^2
+1+\frac{2\Lambda}{3\kappa}
-2\int(1+|x|)p\Phi .
\end{aligned} \tag{11a}
\]
The spline-only terms are rational, and the cross terms are compact integrals enclosed by the \(J\)-equations in the oracle.  Hence (11a) supplies the claimed rational interval for the entire weighted distance.

Finally, even compactly supported rational piecewise-linear functions are dense in the form norm appearing in \(d_\dagger\): first truncate \(\Phi\) using the vanishing tails just proved, then polygonally interpolate on a rational mesh, and finally perturb the finitely many vertex values to rationals.  The interpolation and rational perturbation errors tend to zero in both the derivative norm and the weighted \(L^2\) norm.  The normalized Rayleigh quotient is continuous at the nonzero function \(\Phi\), so there is a candidate \(p\) satisfying
\[
d_\dagger(p,\Phi)^2<2^{-2k},
\qquad Q_\kappa(p)<\Lambda+2^{-k}. \tag{12}
\]
Because the inequalities in (12) are strict, first refine the eigenvalue lower endpoint until \(Q_\kappa(p)<L_\Lambda+2^{-k}\), and then refine the integral intervals until the distance upper endpoint is below \(2^{-2k}\).  The dovetailed enumeration therefore reaches an accepted record.  Its acceptance inequalities and \(L_\Lambda\le\Lambda\) imply
\[
Q_\kappa(\varphi_k^\dagger)
<L_\Lambda+2^{-k}\le\Lambda+2^{-k}. \tag{13}
\]
The distance certificate gives weighted \(H^1\) convergence.  Every integral involving the accepted rational spline is an exact rational polynomial integral, its squared norm is positive, and division by that norm proves all asserted properties of \(w_k^\dagger\).  This proves the lemma.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix integers \(n,k\ge1\), rationals \(\varepsilon,\delta>0\), and a verified spline record from \(\mathrm{def:rational\text{-}airy\text{-}longitudinal\text{-}family}\).  If \(\alpha_n(3T_k^\dagger+2\varepsilon)\le1\), finite-input mode of \(\mathsf E\) terminates.  It returns rational \(b^-\le b^+\) with
\[
b^-\le B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\le b^+,
\qquad b^+-b^-\le\delta,
\qquad
R_n(c^\dagger)\ge B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\ge b^-.
\]
It also returns exact ordered-field maxima of \(G_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)\) on the local, positive-count exterior, and zero-count sets in \(\mathrm{def:evaluator\text{-}handle}\), and an exact rational feasible value \(U\) attained by a total procedure under the fixed independent design \(q^\dagger\), so that \(R_n(c^\dagger)\le U\).  These are same-input finite certificates; no convergence in \(n\) is asserted.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The positivity premise and the exact-primitives proposition make every response probability in the corrected tube nonnegative and make its coordinates sum to one.  Thus \(\nu_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\) is a genuine prior.  On each rational spline piece and sign cell, its integrand is a product of the rational polynomials \(w_k^\dagger\) and \(\rho_\varepsilon\) with integer powers of affine polynomials in \(\alpha_n\).  Exact integration therefore gives, for every response-count vector \(m\),
\[
\nu_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(m)
\in\mathbb Q(\alpha_n). \tag{14}
\]
The orbit likelihood and finite-population target are rational by the exact-primitives proposition.  Hence every denominator, numerator, quotient on a positive-denominator branch, fixed-count Bayes risk, and scaled deficit belongs to \(\mathbb Q(\alpha_n)\).  All indexing sets are finite:
\[
\begin{gathered}
|\mathcal M_{n,3}|<\infty,\quad
|\mathcal R_{n,3}|<\infty,\\
\prod_{a=1}^3(r_a+1)<\infty,\quad
|\mathcal H(m,r,x^{\mathrm{obs}})|<\infty.
\end{gathered} \tag{15}
\]

Represent an element of \(\mathbb Q(\alpha_n)\) by a rational polynomial evaluated at the isolated positive root of \(nX^3-1\), reducing by the square-free factor containing that root.  Euclidean remainder sequences isolate every real root of the numerator polynomial.  Refining the isolating interval for \(\alpha_n\) until it is disjoint from those root intervals decides zero and sign unless the reduced numerator is identically zero, a case detected by its rational coefficients.  Thus every branch, comparison, and finite minimum or maximum in (14)--(15) terminates.  Rational bisection of the selected algebraic Bayes value inside \([0,1]\) terminates with endpoints of width at most \(\delta\), proving the first two displayed inequalities in the statement.

The corrected permutation-orbit Bayes lemma applies because the prior is permutation invariant and the design is outcome independent.  For every design and labeled estimator it gives Bayes risk at least
\[
B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}
=\min_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}
\mathcal B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r). \tag{16}
\]
Maximum risk dominates Bayes risk.  Taking the infimum over the design and estimator in the risk-game definition, then using the returned lower endpoint, yields
\[
R_n(c^\dagger)\ge B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\ge b^-. \tag{17}
\]

For the attaining side, the observation alphabet, action grid, and schedule set in \(\mathrm{def:evaluator\text{-}handle}\) are finite.  Under rational \(q^\dagger\), every coefficient \(P_y(\omega)\{a_j-\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\}^2\) in that linear program is rational.  Enumeration of its finitely many basic feasible solutions and exact rational comparison therefore returns a feasible optimizer \((z,U)\).  The simplex constraints make \(z\) a Markov kernel into \([-1,1]\), hence a total randomized estimator.  Its risk constraint holds for every fixed binary schedule, so its maximum risk is at most \(U\).  Since this fixed independent design is feasible in \(\mathrm{def:risk\text{-}game}\),
\[
R_n(c^\dagger)\le U. \tag{18}
\]
Equations (14)--(18) prove termination and every finite-certificate claim, without making a cross-sample assertion.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(U_n\) be the optimum returned by the rational action-grid program in \(\mathrm{def:evaluator\text{-}handle}\), with \(G=\lceil n^{3/4}\rceil\), under the fixed independent allocation \(q^\dagger\).  Then
\[
R_n(c^\dagger)\le U_n
\le \frac1n-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}n^{-4/3}
+B_{c^\dagger}n^{-3/2}+\frac1{4G^2}.
\]
Consequently the diagonal evaluator's primal error may be chosen to satisfy
\[
e_{\mathrm{pr},n}
\le (B_{c^\dagger}+1/4)n^{-1/6}+2^{-n},
\]
and hence \(e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\to0\) effectively.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The established uniform-risk upper theorem supplies a total estimator \(\delta_n^\star\in[-1,1]\) under independent allocation \(q^\dagger\) and a finite constant \(B_{c^\dagger}\) such that
\[
\max_y\mathbb E\left[
\{\delta_n^\star-\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\}^2\right]
\le \frac1n-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}n^{-4/3}
+B_{c^\dagger}n^{-3/2}. \tag{19}
\]
Fix an observation \(\omega\).  If \(\delta_n^\star(\omega)\in[a_j,a_{j+1}]\), choose a randomized grid action \(A_\omega\in\{a_j,a_{j+1}\}\) whose conditional mean is \(\delta_n^\star(\omega)\).  For every target value \(\tau\in[-1,1]\), conditional square completion gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E\{(A_\omega-\tau)^2\mid\omega\}
&=\{\delta_n^\star(\omega)-\tau\}^2
+\operatorname{Var}(A_\omega\mid\omega)\\
&\le\{\delta_n^\star(\omega)-\tau\}^2
+\frac{(a_{j+1}-a_j)^2}{4}\\
&=\{\delta_n^\star(\omega)-\tau\}^2+\frac1{4G^2}.
\end{aligned} \tag{20}
\]
The randomized kernel in (20) is feasible for the grid linear program.  Since \(U_n\) is its minimum and the independent design is feasible in the unrestricted risk game, (19)--(20) imply
\[
R_n(c^\dagger)\le U_n
\le\frac1n-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}n^{-4/3}
+B_{c^\dagger}n^{-3/2}+\frac1{4G^2}. \tag{21}
\]
Because \(G\ge n^{3/4}\), multiplying the last two remainder terms by \(n^{4/3}\) bounds them by
\[
B_{c^\dagger}n^{-1/6}+\frac14n^{-1/6}. \tag{22}
\]
Diagonal-output mode refines the rational upper endpoint for \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\) to within \(2^{-n}\).  Its outward definition of \(e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\), combined with (21)--(22), proves the asserted computable bound and convergence.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), there is one Turing machine extending \(\mathsf E\) with the following properties.  On input \(n\), for all sufficiently large \(n\), it outputs an index \(k_n\), the complete verified spline record for \(\varphi_{k_n}^\dagger\), a rational \(\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}>0\), rational nonnegative errors
\(e_{\mathrm{loc},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{shell},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\), and \(e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\), and finite ordered-field certificates.  The outputs satisfy
\[
k_n\uparrow\infty,\qquad \varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}\downarrow0,\qquad
\alpha_n(3T_{k_n}^\dagger+2\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A})\le1.
\]
For
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal L_n&=\left\{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}:\min_a r_a>0,
\ \left\|n^{1/6}(r/n-q^\dagger)\right\|_\infty\le n^{1/72}\right\},\\
\mathcal X_n&=\{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}:\min_a r_a>0\}\setminus\mathcal L_n,\\
\mathcal Z_n&=\{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}:\min_a r_a=0\},
\end{aligned}
\]
the certified all-count conclusions are
\[
\begin{aligned}
G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
&\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_{\mathrm{loc},n}&& (r\in\mathcal L_n),\\
G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
&\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_{\mathrm{shell},n}&& (r\in\mathcal X_n),\\
G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
&\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_{\mathrm{zero},n}&& (r\in\mathcal Z_n).
\end{aligned} \tag{A}
\]
The same output contains a total finite procedure \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm A}\) satisfying
\[
\max_{y\in\{0,1\}^{n\times3}}
\mathbb E\left[\{\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm A}-
\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\}^2\right]
\le n^{-1}-\{\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\}n^{-4/3}. \tag{B}
\]
It also outputs a code for a rational-valued nonincreasing computable function \(E\) such that \(E(N)\to0\) and, for every \(n\ge N\),
\[
\max\{e_{\mathrm{loc},n},e_{\mathrm{shell},n},
e_{\mathrm{zero},n},e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\}\le E(N). \tag{C}
\]
The inequalities (A)--(C), including exterior and zero-count control, are theorem conclusions and are not inputs or assumptions.  They imply the finite certified squeeze
\[
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-e_{\mathrm{pr},n}
\le n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-R_n(c^\dagger)\}
\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+
\max\{e_{\mathrm{loc},n},e_{\mathrm{shell},n},e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\},
\]
and consequently
\[
R_n(c^\dagger)=n^{-1}-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}),
\qquad
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\in(0,\infty).
\]
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current claim still asserts coefficient arrays, widening-prior schedules, and a finite limit for the polynomial density refuted by the exact Horvitz--Thompson Bayes-risk witness. The corrected claim restricts the bridge to the exact rational Airy-tube prior, replaces the obsolete coefficient by the independently defined value \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\), and keeps local, exterior, zero-face, primal, and computable-tail control as conclusions rather than hypotheses.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Put \(\kappa=\kappa(c^\dagger)=5/8\), \(\Phi=\phi_{c^\dagger}\), and \(\Lambda=\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\).  The rational interval Airy oracle is the following certified procedure.  For an integer \(R\ge1\), let \(\lambda_N(R)\) and \(\lambda_D(R)\) be the lowest Rayleigh quotients of
\[
4\int_0^R|f'(x)|^2\,dx+\kappa\int_0^R x f(x)^2\,dx
\]
under \(f'(0)=0\) and, respectively, \(f'(R)=0\) or \(f(R)=0\).  It encloses these two simple eigenvalues by shooting the initial-value equation
\[
W'(x)=A(x,\lambda)W(x),\qquad
A(x,\lambda)=
\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\(\kappa x-\lambda)/4&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
W(0)=(1,0)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
On a rational step \([x_0,x_0+h]\), Picard iterates are integrated coefficientwise.  If the rational number \(L\) bounds \(\|A(x,\lambda)\|_\infty\) on the current rational box, the order-\(m\) remainder is enclosed by
\[
\|W(x_0)\|_\infty e^{L|h|}
\frac{(L|h|)^{m+1}}{(m+1)!};
\]
the exponential is enclosed by its rational Taylor series and its geometric tail after increasing \(m\) until the tail ratio is below one.  The same iteration is applied to the \(\lambda\)-derivative equation.  Rational interval Newton steps, together with interval sign checks for \(W_1\) on the preceding mesh cells, isolate the first Dirichlet and Neumann zeros.  Increase \(R\), the mesh resolution, and \(m\) until rational numbers \(L_\Lambda<U_\Lambda\) satisfy
\[
L_\Lambda\le \min\{\lambda_N(R),\kappa R\}
\le\Lambda\le\lambda_D(R)\le U_\Lambda,
\qquad U_\Lambda-L_\Lambda<2^{-p}.
\]
Starting from the interval initial data
\[
\Phi(0)=\sqrt{\kappa/(2\Lambda)},\qquad \Phi'(0)=0,
\]
the oracle augments the system by
\[
I_0'=\Phi^2,\qquad I_1'=x\Phi^2,\qquad I_2'=(\Phi')^2
\]
and, on every proposed spline piece, by
\[
J_0'=p\Phi,\qquad J_1'=xp\Phi,\qquad J_2'=p'\Phi'.
\]
It returns rational interval enclosures of \(\Phi\), \(\Phi'\), these compact integrals, and the tails obtained from
\[
\int_{\mathbb R}(\Phi')^2=\frac{\Lambda}{12},\qquad
\int_{\mathbb R}|x|\Phi^2=\frac{2\Lambda}{3\kappa},\qquad
\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi^2=1.
\]
It increases \(R\) and the internal precision until the requested compact and weighted-tail enclosure widths are below \(2^{-p}\).

Enumerate by natural-number code all pairs \((T,p)\) in which \(T\) is a positive integer and \(p\) is a nonzero, even, continuous rational piecewise-linear function supported in \([-T,T]\).  For such \(p\), put
\[
d_\dagger(p,\Phi)^2=
\int_{\mathbb R}\left\{|p'-\Phi'|^2+(1+|x|)|p-\Phi|^2\right\}dx
\]
and define the normalized Rayleigh quotient
\[
Q_\kappa(p)=
\frac{4\int_{\mathbb R}|p'|^2dx+
\kappa\int_{\mathbb R}|x|p^2dx}
{\int_{\mathbb R}p^2dx}.
\]
For each \(k\ge1\), dovetail the spline enumeration and oracle precisions.  Accept the first coded candidate for which interval arithmetic certifies the strict inequalities
\[
d_\dagger(p,\Phi)^2<2^{-2k},
\qquad Q_\kappa(p)<L_\Lambda+2^{-k}.
\]
The complete output record contains the code, \(T\), every rational breakpoint and affine coefficient of \(p\), the exact rational values of the three spline integrals in \(Q_\kappa(p)\), the exact quotient, the eigenvalue bracket, the interval upper bound for \(d_\dagger(p,\Phi)^2\), the ODE mesh and Picard orders, and the compact-integral and weighted-tail intervals.  Define \(T_k^\dagger=T\), \(\varphi_k^\dagger=p\), and
\[
w_k^\dagger(x)=
\frac{(\varphi_k^\dagger(x))^2}
{\int_{\mathbb R}(\varphi_k^\dagger(z))^2dz}.
\]
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The former first-pair rule tests a non-strict inequality involving the unknown ground state and therefore is not a terminating algorithm. The corrected construction uses rational Sturm shooting, validated Picard/Taylor remainders, exact flux and virial tail identities, strict interval acceptance, a complete replayable record, and the normalized Rayleigh quotient required by the directive.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
The evaluator \(\mathsf E\) has a finite-input mode and a diagonal-output mode.  In finite-input mode its inputs are integers \(n,k\ge1\), rationals \(\varepsilon,\delta>0\), and the complete verified spline record returned by \(\mathrm{def:rational\text{-}airy\text{-}longitudinal\text{-}family}\).  It first replays every rational interval check in that record and verifies
\[
\alpha_n(3T_k^\dagger+2\varepsilon)\le1.
\]
It then integrates each rational spline piece and each sign cell in \(\mathrm{def:explicit\text{-}three\text{-}arm\text{-}airy\text{-}tube}\), enumerates the finite sets of response counts \(m\), allocation counts \(r\), observations \(x^{\mathrm{obs}}\), and factorial tables \(H\), and evaluates every weight and posterior-risk term in the ordered real algebraic field \(\mathbb Q(\alpha_n)\).  It returns rational endpoints \(b^-\le b^+\) satisfying
\[
b^-\le B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\le b^+,
\qquad b^+-b^-\le\delta,
\]
together with exact ordered-field certificates for every comparison and for the maximum of \(G_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)\) on each of the following three disjoint sets:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal L_n&=\left\{r:\min_a r_a>0,
\ \left\|n^{1/6}(r/n-q^\dagger)\right\|_\infty
\le n^{1/72}\right\},\\
\mathcal X_n&=\{r:\min_a r_a>0\}\setminus\mathcal L_n,\\
\mathcal Z_n&=\{r:\min_a r_a=0\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
For the attaining certificate, let \(\mathcal O_n\) be the finite observation alphabet under independent assignment with allocation \(q^\dagger\), let \(a_j=-1+j/G\), \(0\le j\le2G\), and solve the rational linear program in variables \(z_{\omega j}\) and \(U\):
\[
\begin{gathered}
\text{minimize }U\quad\text{subject to}\\
z_{\omega j}\ge0,\quad \sum_{j=0}^{2G}z_{\omega j}=1
\quad(\omega\in\mathcal O_n),\\
\sum_{\omega\in\mathcal O_n}\sum_{j=0}^{2G}
P_y(\omega)z_{\omega j}\{a_j-\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\}^2\le U
\quad\text{for every }y\in\{0,1\}^{n\times3}.
\end{gathered}
\]
Here \(G=\lceil n^{3/4}\rceil\) and \(P_y\) is the rational observation law under \(q^\dagger\).  The returned feasible optimizer is a total randomized estimator and \(U\) is its exact rational worst-case-risk certificate.

In diagonal-output mode, on input \(n\), the same Turing machine generates the complete records for \(1\le j\le n\), refines the Airy eigenvalue interval to width at most \(2^{-n}\), puts \(\varepsilon_j=2^{-j}\), and selects the largest \(j\le n\) for which
\(\alpha_n(3T_j^\dagger+2\varepsilon_j)\le1\), reporting an inadmissibility flag only when this finite set is empty.  It calls finite-input mode at the selected index and outputs rational outward upper errors \(e_{\mathrm{loc},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{shell},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\), and \(e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\).  The first three enclose the positive parts of the corresponding three exact maxima minus the current lower endpoint \(L_\Lambda\); the last encloses
\[
\left[n^{4/3}\{U-n^{-1}\}+U_\Lambda\right]_+.
\]
The finite-input and per-sample diagonal modes are total.  A cross-sample certificate consists additionally of a code for a rational-valued, nonincreasing computable function \(E\) on \(\mathbb N\), finite certificates that all four errors are at most \(E(N)\) whenever \(n\ge N\), and a certificate that \(E(N)\to0\).  Termination and correctness of this cross-sample extension are conclusions required of \(\mathrm{thm:unequal\text{-}three\text{-}arm\text{-}allocation\text{-}tube}\), not conditions supplied to the evaluator.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The former evaluator is tied to the refuted widening density and asserts an unproved cross-sample stopping rule. The corrected construction takes the verified Airy spline record explicitly, proves only finite-input and per-sample termination by exact enumeration, exposes the local, exterior, zero-face, and primal errors, and leaves the vanishing tail majorant to the root theorem.

proposed.name: Effective compact rational Airy longitudinal family
proposed.construction:
Put \(\kappa=\kappa(c^\dagger)=5/8\), \(\Phi=\phi_{c^\dagger}\), and \(\Lambda=\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\).  The rational interval Airy oracle is the following certified procedure.  For an integer \(R\ge1\), let \(\lambda_N(R)\) and \(\lambda_D(R)\) be the lowest Rayleigh quotients of
\[
4\int_0^R|f'(x)|^2\,dx+\kappa\int_0^R x f(x)^2\,dx
\]
under \(f'(0)=0\) and, respectively, \(f'(R)=0\) or \(f(R)=0\).  It encloses these two simple eigenvalues by shooting the initial-value equation
\[
W'(x)=A(x,\lambda)W(x),\qquad
A(x,\lambda)=
\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\(\kappa x-\lambda)/4&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
W(0)=(1,0)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
On a rational step \([x_0,x_0+h]\), Picard iterates are integrated coefficientwise.  If the rational number \(L\) bounds \(\|A(x,\lambda)\|_\infty\) on the current rational box, the order-\(m\) remainder is enclosed by
\[
\|W(x_0)\|_\infty e^{L|h|}
\frac{(L|h|)^{m+1}}{(m+1)!};
\]
the exponential is enclosed by its rational Taylor series and its geometric tail after increasing \(m\) until the tail ratio is below one.  The same iteration is applied to the \(\lambda\)-derivative equation.  Rational interval Newton steps, together with interval sign checks for \(W_1\) on the preceding mesh cells, isolate the first Dirichlet and Neumann zeros.  Increase \(R\), the mesh resolution, and \(m\) until rational numbers \(L_\Lambda<U_\Lambda\) satisfy
\[
L_\Lambda\le \min\{\lambda_N(R),\kappa R\}
\le\Lambda\le\lambda_D(R)\le U_\Lambda,
\qquad U_\Lambda-L_\Lambda<2^{-p}.
\]
Starting from the interval initial data
\[
\Phi(0)=\sqrt{\kappa/(2\Lambda)},\qquad \Phi'(0)=0,
\]
the oracle augments the system by
\[
I_0'=\Phi^2,\qquad I_1'=x\Phi^2,\qquad I_2'=(\Phi')^2
\]
and, on every proposed spline piece, by
\[
J_0'=p\Phi,\qquad J_1'=xp\Phi,\qquad J_2'=p'\Phi'.
\]
It returns rational interval enclosures of \(\Phi\), \(\Phi'\), these compact integrals, and the tails obtained from
\[
\int_{\mathbb R}(\Phi')^2=\frac{\Lambda}{12},\qquad
\int_{\mathbb R}|x|\Phi^2=\frac{2\Lambda}{3\kappa},\qquad
\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi^2=1.
\]
It increases \(R\) and the internal precision until the requested compact and weighted-tail enclosure widths are below \(2^{-p}\).

Enumerate by natural-number code all pairs \((T,p)\) in which \(T\) is a positive integer and \(p\) is a nonzero, even, continuous rational piecewise-linear function supported in \([-T,T]\).  For such \(p\), put
\[
d_\dagger(p,\Phi)^2=
\int_{\mathbb R}\left\{|p'-\Phi'|^2+(1+|x|)|p-\Phi|^2\right\}dx
\]
and define the normalized Rayleigh quotient
\[
Q_\kappa(p)=
\frac{4\int_{\mathbb R}|p'|^2dx+
\kappa\int_{\mathbb R}|x|p^2dx}
{\int_{\mathbb R}p^2dx}.
\]
For each \(k\ge1\), dovetail the spline enumeration and oracle precisions.  Accept the first coded candidate for which interval arithmetic certifies the strict inequalities
\[
d_\dagger(p,\Phi)^2<2^{-2k},
\qquad Q_\kappa(p)<L_\Lambda+2^{-k}.
\]
The complete output record contains the code, \(T\), every rational breakpoint and affine coefficient of \(p\), the exact rational values of the three spline integrals in \(Q_\kappa(p)\), the exact quotient, the eigenvalue bracket, the interval upper bound for \(d_\dagger(p,\Phi)^2\), the ODE mesh and Picard orders, and the compact-integral and weighted-tail intervals.  Define \(T_k^\dagger=T\), \(\varphi_k^\dagger=p\), and
\[
w_k^\dagger(x)=
\frac{(\varphi_k^\dagger(x))^2}
{\int_{\mathbb R}(\varphi_k^\dagger(z))^2dz}.
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: The construction and its metadata must move together because the effective oracle now uses the Airy eigenvalue and outputs a replayable normalized-energy certificate.

proposed.name: Corrected Airy finite-input and diagonal evaluation handle
proposed.construction:
The evaluator \(\mathsf E\) has a finite-input mode and a diagonal-output mode.  In finite-input mode its inputs are integers \(n,k\ge1\), rationals \(\varepsilon,\delta>0\), and the complete verified spline record returned by \(\mathrm{def:rational\text{-}airy\text{-}longitudinal\text{-}family}\).  It first replays every rational interval check in that record and verifies
\[
\alpha_n(3T_k^\dagger+2\varepsilon)\le1.
\]
It then integrates each rational spline piece and each sign cell in \(\mathrm{def:explicit\text{-}three\text{-}arm\text{-}airy\text{-}tube}\), enumerates the finite sets of response counts \(m\), allocation counts \(r\), observations \(x^{\mathrm{obs}}\), and factorial tables \(H\), and evaluates every weight and posterior-risk term in the ordered real algebraic field \(\mathbb Q(\alpha_n)\).  It returns rational endpoints \(b^-\le b^+\) satisfying
\[
b^-\le B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\le b^+,
\qquad b^+-b^-\le\delta,
\]
together with exact ordered-field certificates for every comparison and for the maximum of \(G_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)\) on each of the following three disjoint sets:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal L_n&=\left\{r:\min_a r_a>0,
\ \left\|n^{1/6}(r/n-q^\dagger)\right\|_\infty
\le n^{1/72}\right\},\\
\mathcal X_n&=\{r:\min_a r_a>0\}\setminus\mathcal L_n,\\
\mathcal Z_n&=\{r:\min_a r_a=0\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
For the attaining certificate, let \(\mathcal O_n\) be the finite observation alphabet under independent assignment with allocation \(q^\dagger\), let \(a_j=-1+j/G\), \(0\le j\le2G\), and solve the rational linear program in variables \(z_{\omega j}\) and \(U\):
\[
\begin{gathered}
\text{minimize }U\quad\text{subject to}\\
z_{\omega j}\ge0,\quad \sum_{j=0}^{2G}z_{\omega j}=1
\quad(\omega\in\mathcal O_n),\\
\sum_{\omega\in\mathcal O_n}\sum_{j=0}^{2G}
P_y(\omega)z_{\omega j}\{a_j-\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\}^2\le U
\quad\text{for every }y\in\{0,1\}^{n\times3}.
\end{gathered}
\]
Here \(G=\lceil n^{3/4}\rceil\) and \(P_y\) is the rational observation law under \(q^\dagger\).  The returned feasible optimizer is a total randomized estimator and \(U\) is its exact rational worst-case-risk certificate.

In diagonal-output mode, on input \(n\), the same Turing machine generates the complete records for \(1\le j\le n\), refines the Airy eigenvalue interval to width at most \(2^{-n}\), puts \(\varepsilon_j=2^{-j}\), and selects the largest \(j\le n\) for which
\(\alpha_n(3T_j^\dagger+2\varepsilon_j)\le1\), reporting an inadmissibility flag only when this finite set is empty.  It calls finite-input mode at the selected index and outputs rational outward upper errors \(e_{\mathrm{loc},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{shell},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\), and \(e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\).  The first three enclose the positive parts of the corresponding three exact maxima minus the current lower endpoint \(L_\Lambda\); the last encloses
\[
\left[n^{4/3}\{U-n^{-1}\}+U_\Lambda\right]_+.
\]
The finite-input and per-sample diagonal modes are total.  A cross-sample certificate consists additionally of a code for a rational-valued, nonincreasing computable function \(E\) on \(\mathbb N\), finite certificates that all four errors are at most \(E(N)\) whenever \(n\ge N\), and a certificate that \(E(N)\to0\).  Termination and correctness of this cross-sample extension are conclusions required of \(\mathrm{thm:unequal\text{-}three\text{-}arm\text{-}allocation\text{-}tube}\), not conditions supplied to the evaluator.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The evaluator now consumes the corrected Airy record and exact corrected-prior quantities; the obsolete widening schedules and certificate symbols are removed from its metadata.

The old helper certifies an unnormalized numerator and selects a first spline using a non-effective non-strict comparison. The replacement proves the stronger effective record and the required normalized quotient.

proposed.statement:
For \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), there is one Turing machine extending \(\mathsf E\) with the following properties.  On input \(n\), for all sufficiently large \(n\), it outputs an index \(k_n\), the complete verified spline record for \(\varphi_{k_n}^\dagger\), a rational \(\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}>0\), rational nonnegative errors
\(e_{\mathrm{loc},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{shell},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\), and \(e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\), and finite ordered-field certificates.  The outputs satisfy
\[
k_n\uparrow\infty,\qquad \varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}\downarrow0,\qquad
\alpha_n(3T_{k_n}^\dagger+2\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A})\le1.
\]
For
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal L_n&=\left\{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}:\min_a r_a>0,
\ \left\|n^{1/6}(r/n-q^\dagger)\right\|_\infty\le n^{1/72}\right\},\\
\mathcal X_n&=\{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}:\min_a r_a>0\}\setminus\mathcal L_n,\\
\mathcal Z_n&=\{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}:\min_a r_a=0\},
\end{aligned}
\]
the certified all-count conclusions are
\[
\begin{aligned}
G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
&\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_{\mathrm{loc},n}&& (r\in\mathcal L_n),\\
G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
&\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_{\mathrm{shell},n}&& (r\in\mathcal X_n),\\
G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
&\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_{\mathrm{zero},n}&& (r\in\mathcal Z_n).
\end{aligned} \tag{A}
\]
The same output contains a total finite procedure \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm A}\) satisfying
\[
\max_{y\in\{0,1\}^{n\times3}}
\mathbb E\left[\{\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm A}-
\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\}^2\right]
\le n^{-1}-\{\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\}n^{-4/3}. \tag{B}
\]
It also outputs a code for a rational-valued nonincreasing computable function \(E\) such that \(E(N)\to0\) and, for every \(n\ge N\),
\[
\max\{e_{\mathrm{loc},n},e_{\mathrm{shell},n},
e_{\mathrm{zero},n},e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\}\le E(N). \tag{C}
\]
The inequalities (A)--(C), including exterior and zero-count control, are theorem conclusions and are not inputs or assumptions.  They imply the finite certified squeeze
\[
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-e_{\mathrm{pr},n}
\le n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-R_n(c^\dagger)\}
\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+
\max\{e_{\mathrm{loc},n},e_{\mathrm{shell},n},e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\},
\]
and consequently
\[
R_n(c^\dagger)=n^{-1}-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}),
\qquad
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\in(0,\infty).
\]
proposed.justification: This is the corrected-prior all-count bridge whose certified tail majorant would identify the unrestricted second-order constant at the designated unequal three-arm contrast.
proposed.gap: Finite exact enumeration does not prove that the local, positive-count exterior, and zero-count Bayes-deficit maxima converge uniformly to the Airy value; a boundary-valid likelihood or Bayes-information expansion with a computable common remainder is still required.
proposed.consumer: A prospective unequal three-regimen binary-endpoint design may use the proved fixed-independent benchmark and fixed-input intervals, while the unrestricted equality remains unavailable until this bridge is proved.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The dependency spine must use the corrected Airy family, normalized effective record, corrected fixed-input evaluator, and Airy constant, with no widening-prior extractor or widening schedules.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: \(R_n(c^\dagger)=n^{-1}-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\), where \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\) is the independently defined Airy value and is to be certified by the corrected all-count diagonal
proposed_core_edits.reason: The advertised unrestricted equality is preserved, as directed, but its constant must be rebased from the refuted widening-prior coefficient \(\mathfrak L^\dagger\) to the corrected Airy value \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove the lower-bound parts of conclusions (A)--(C) of the corrected target: one design-independent corrected Airy-tube diagonal must bound the fixed-count Bayes deficit uniformly on the \(n^{-1/6}\) local allocation face, every positive-count exterior allocation, and every zero-count face, and these three errors must admit one computable monotone tail majorant tending to zero.
open_obligations.obstruction: The exact evaluator only computes each finite Bayes maximum. Neither the frozen core nor the presolve supplies a target-specific Bayes-information identity or a likelihood expansion with a remainder uniform in allocation counts, spline index, transverse width, rare response types, posterior denominators, and boundary faces. Finite enumeration at each \(n\) cannot certify a statement for every future sample size. Assuming those bounds or the tail majorant would assume the theorem's crux. The primal error is not part of the obstruction: the rational-grid lemma gives it an explicit vanishing bound.
open_obligations.attempted: The widening polynomial prior was refuted by an exact Horvitz--Thompson Bayes-risk calculation. The longitudinal family was replaced by an effective rational spline-square approximation with a normalized-energy certificate; prior positivity, the exact finite-population target, permutation-orbit reduction, posterior square completion, and all finite allocation-stratum maxima were verified at every fixed admissible input. Randomized barycentric rounding of the established Airy estimator proves the matching total rational primal error is at most \((B_{c^\dagger}+1/4)n^{-1/6}+2^{-n}\). These steps do not control the cross-sample posterior quotient, especially when allocation counts approach zero.
open_obligations.partial_result: The effective normalized Airy-record lemma proves a uniform algorithm \(k\mapsto(T_k^\dagger,\varphi_k^\dagger,w_k^\dagger,\text{record})\), using only rational interval ODE/Taylor calculations and certified weighted tails.  For each fixed admissible \((n,k,\varepsilon,\delta)\), the corrected finite-input evaluator terminates, computes the exact ordered-field Bayes certificate and all three allocation-stratum maxima, and returns a total rational finite procedure.  The permutation-orbit lemma gives \(R_n(c^\dagger)\ge B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\).  Randomized barycentric rounding and the established fixed-design theorem give the independently proved attaining coefficient \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\) with the effective primal error bound \(e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\le(B_{c^\dagger}+1/4)n^{-1/6}+2^{-n}\).  What remains is cross-sample, design-uniform control of the three computed Bayes lower-bound errors.

prose_updates.tldr: For \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), the proved sharp result is currently the fixed-independent-design expansion with coefficient \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\), together with the corresponding one-sided lower limit for the unrestricted deficit. The former widening polynomial tube is exactly refuted. Its replacement is an effective compact rational Airy spline-square prior: a rational interval ODE/Taylor oracle certifies the normalized energy and weighted tails, and a fixed-input evaluator computes exact ordered-field Bayes intervals and finite allocation-stratum maxima. The unrestricted sharp equality remains the target; its design-uniform all-count bridge and computable cross-sample tail majorant are open.

project_justification.gap: The accepted parent proves the \(n^{-4/3}\) order and finite response-type programs, while the proved fixed-independent theorem identifies the Airy coefficient. No available result gives the reverse inequality for every outcome-independent dependent design. The missing step is a uniform corrected-prior Bayes bridge covering \(n^{-1/6}\) allocation perturbations, all positive-count exterior allocations, and zero-count faces with one effective remainder.
project_justification.niche: At \(c^\dagger\), all eight response types and a nonzero transverse nuisance direction are needed because a scalar-path prior can be exploited by a pair-focused design. The scientifically meaningful unresolved question is whether unrestricted designs improve on the fixed allocation \(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\) at second order.
project_justification.fill: The current verified contribution gives the exact response-alphabet geometry, a total fixed-independent Airy procedure, an effective normalized rational Airy-record algorithm, a genuine corrected transverse prior at every admissible input, an exact permutation-orbit Bayes reduction, and a terminating same-input ordered-algebraic evaluator. The proposed root theorem now states the precise all-count inequalities and monotone tail certificate still needed for the unrestricted sharp equality.

sampling_model.design: The causal game permits every outcome-independent assignment law, including dependence across labeled units and zero allocation to an arm. The proved comparator assigns units independently with \(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\). The corrected prior is selected independently of the design, and the orbit reduction is exact at every fixed allocation count; uniform optimization over all counts remains open.
sampling_model.overlap: No overlap condition is imposed on the unrestricted design. Positive local counts, positive exterior counts, and zero-count faces are separate required conclusions of the corrected bridge, so boundary allocations cannot be discarded by assumption.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no superpopulation nuisance estimation. The compact transverse coordinate is a design-independent prior device orthogonal to the finite-population contrast; shrinking it while retaining uniform control of posterior denominators and allocation boundaries is part of the open proof.

prose_updates.related_work: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026) provide the scalar two-arm Airy benchmark and feedback bounds, not a three-active-arm all-design converse. Hull (2026) is likewise a two-arm unrestricted result. The accepted parent supplies the exact finite orbit game, first-order value, second-order order, and same-sample certificates. The present verified steps adapt the spectral computation to a replayable rational interval ODE/Taylor oracle and carry a corrected nonzero-transverse prior through exact fixed-input evaluation. Hirano and Porter (2009) and Levit (1986) remain methodological comparators; neither is invoked as the missing finite-population, allocation-uniform bridge. Hammer et al. (1996) supplies only prospective complete binary-endpoint regimen-trial motivation, not a censored-outcome reanalysis.
prose_updates.interpretation: For a prospective fixed-horizon three-regimen trial with a prespecified binary endpoint and contrast \(1:-1/4:-3/4\), the independent allocation \(q^\dagger\) and its nonlinear Airy correction have a proved sharp second-order value within that fixed design. Exact finite corrected-prior intervals can be computed at a planned sample size. They must not yet be interpreted as certificates that no dependent or otherwise nonstandard outcome-independent design has a smaller worst-case risk.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact \(K=3,n=3\) full-label gap and the defeat of scalar-path priors do not determine the asymptotic design gap. The widening polynomial density is unusable because its exact scaled Bayes deficit grows at least linearly in its truncation radius. The corrected rational Airy family removes that obstruction and is effectively generated, but same-input exact maxima do not yield a cross-sample modulus. A proof must still expand the exact posterior risk uniformly through rare-type and zero-allocation boundaries; no Gaussian, Taylor, or normal-limit statement is assumed.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The unrestricted sharp equality at \(c^\dagger\) remains the advertised estimand functional but is open. Proved results are the fixed-independent sharp expansion, the unrestricted one-sided deficit bound, the effective normalized Airy record, and fixed-input exact Bayes and primal certificates. No growing-\(K\), uniform vanishing-weight, arbitrary-real computability, or equality-versus-strict-loss conclusion is claimed. The corrected root theorem is restricted to \(c^\dagger\) and requires a single verified machine with a monotone computable tail majorant; finite numerical extrapolation is not a substitute.

statement_notes.justification: This is the corrected Airy-prior all-count bridge that would turn fixed-input orbit certificates into the unrestricted sharp second-order value.
statement_notes.gap: The effective spline record and exact evaluator do not bound their computed local, exterior, and zero-face errors uniformly in \(n\); the target-specific posterior-risk expansion and computable tail majorant remain unproved.
statement_notes.consumer: A trial designer may use the fixed-independent benchmark and same-input intervals, but not the unrestricted equality, until this theorem closes.
